title: A Hybrid CPU-GPU Approach for Memory-Efficient Volume Rendering of Medical Image Data
abstract: Volume rendering based on 3D texture mapping is widely used in CT/MRI medical imaging, but constrained by GPU memory bottlenecks.While greedy packing strategies, which pack sub-textures into the first available empty space to minimise gaps, are effective in 2D texture mapping, adapting them to native 3D texture mapping introduces memory inflation due to the hardware constraint requiring uniform texture dimensions.This paper presents a CPU-GPU hybrid pipeline that mitigates this issue through a novel post-packing optimisation to minimise memory waste, with CPU pre-processing and GPU rendering.Experimental results demonstrate an average 30.9%reduction in memory usage compared to the default 3D texture mapping baseline, achieving memory-efficient rendering without compromising visual quality.
